title: Seat holds during checkout
description: A ticketing service must let a user select a seat, spend up to 10 minutes entering payment details, then buy it, with no seat ever sold twice. Payment authorization takes 1 to 8 seconds. Which design is most appropriate?

options.text: SELECT the seat FOR UPDATE when the user selects it and keep the transaction open until payment completes
options.explanation: Holding a row lock across minutes of user think time and a remote payment call exhausts connections, blocks other readers of the row and leaves locks dangling when clients disappear.

options.text: Atomically move the seat from available to held with a holder and expiry via a conditional update, then convert held to sold only if the hold is still yours and unexpired
options.explanation: Each transition is a single conditional write in the authoritative database, so concurrent buyers cannot both win, and abandoned holds become available again when the TTL passes.

options.text: Check availability in a Redis cache and write the sale to the database when payment succeeds
options.explanation: The cache check and database write are separate steps, so two buyers can both see the seat as free and both complete payment.

options.text: Use optimistic concurrency with a version column, checked only at purchase time
options.explanation: Correct at commit, but on a popular seat many users spend 10 minutes filling in payment only to lose at the end; there is no hold to tell others the seat is taken.
